mainTopic: Does a person's hand count as a place of four by four טפחים for עקירה and הנחה on שבת? The amud then turns to related rulings about catching, throwing, and gathering rainwater.
overview: The גמרא wants to know how the משנה can make someone liable when an object is lifted from a hand or placed into one, since עקירה and הנחה normally need a place of four by four טפחים. It tries to match the משנה to רבי and then to אחרים, but rejects both. רבי אבא says the object was really in a basket held in the hand. רבי אבהו objects to adding a basket and says the hand was held within three טפחים of the ground. רבא rejects these forced cases and gives a simple rule: a person's hand counts as four by four, and רבי יוחנן said the same. רבי יוחנן adds that a hand counts even when its owner did not choose to use it, and that the thrower is liable only if the catcher stood still. He asks what happens if the thrower runs and catches the object himself, and the question ends with תיקו. Finally, the גמרא discusses catching rainwater in a friend's חצר and explains it as actively gathering the water from a sloped wall. It then starts to quote the משנה where רבא first spoke about a sloped wall, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי's leniency only applies in a covered private domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects matching the משנה to רבי. רבי only makes a person liable without a real four-טפחים surface in a covered רשות היחיד, where the whole house counts as 'full'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי only makes a person liable in a covered private domain, because we say a house is treated as if it is filled up. But in a private domain that is not covered, he does not make him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had suggested that the משנה follows רבי, who seemed not to need a מקום ארבעה. Now it rejects that suggestion by limiting what רבי actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי makes a thrower liable even when the object lands on a tiny ledge, but only inside a roofed private area. A roofed house is treated as one solid unit, as if it were filled up, so any spot inside counts as a proper resting place. That reasoning does not apply to an open area, so רבי gives no general proof that a hand can count as a resting place.

keyTerms.meaning: A house is considered as if it is filled up

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying that a four-טפחים area is unnecessary. He is saying that in a roofed house, the whole space already counts as a valid four-טפחים area.

phrases.english: Rebbi does not hold one liable
except in a covered private domain,
as we say:
A house is considered as though it is full.
phrases.notes: So any point inside it counts as a resting surface.

phrases.english: But one that is not covered — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי אֶלָּא בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד מְקוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attribution of the משנה to רבי that the earlier part of the daf proposed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to use רבי as the source for not needing a מקום ארבעה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's ruling depends on a covered domain being treated as 'full'. It is not a general rule that a four-טפחים area is unnecessary.

steps.title: Could the משנה also be about a covered area?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers saying that the משנה also speaks of a covered area. It objects that this might work for a covered private domain, but would the person really be liable in a covered public domain?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too the משנה speaks of a covered area: that works for a covered private domain, but is a person liable at all in a covered public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the link to רבי by saying the משנה also deals with a roofed area. It immediately questions that idea, and the next step brings the source behind the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in the משנה involves both a private domain and a public domain. A roof could help on the private side. But if the public side were also roofed, there might be no liability at all, so this escape route creates a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)
That works for... (granted in one case, but...)

phrases.english: And if you will say
here too it is speaking of a covered area
that works for a covered private domain,
but in a covered public domain, is he liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible way to keep the רבי attribution, then challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה is speaking of a covered area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes people liable in the public domain too, but a covered public domain may not create liability at all.

steps.title: רב: no liability in a covered public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its challenge with רב's ruling: carrying four אמות in a covered רשות הרבים is פטור, because it is not like the camp formations (דגלי מדבר) in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב שמואל בר יהודה said in the name of רבי אבא, in the name of רב הונא, in the name of רב: one who carries an object four אמות in a covered public domain is exempt, because it is not like the camp formations in the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that proves the challenge from the previous step. A covered public domain does not create liability, so the משנה cannot be about one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of carrying on שבת are learned from how בני ישראל carried in the open camp in the desert, which had no roof. A roofed public area does not match that model, so carrying there is פטור. As a result, saying 'the משנה is about a covered area' cannot rescue the attribution to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries an object four cubits
The camp formations of the tribes in the desert
But didn't (so-and-so) say? (brings a source against an idea)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the laws of הוצאה are modeled on the open desert camp. A roof can change whether an area counts as a real רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who carries an object four cubits
in a covered public domain is exempt —
because it is not similar to the banners of the desert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up the challenge in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a covered public domain does not create liability
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling, passed down through a chain of אמוראים, about carrying four אמות in a covered רשות הרבים

steps.title: רבי זירא: the משנה follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא proposes a new source: the משנה follows אחרים. In their ברייתא, a thrower is liable if the receiver stood in place and caught the object, and exempt if the receiver moved to catch it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: Whose opinion is this משנה? It is אחרים. As it was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say, if the receiver stood in his place and caught it, the thrower is liable. If he moved from his place and caught it, the thrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the attempt with רבי failed, רבי זירא suggests a different תנא whose view fits the משנה. He quotes the ברייתא of אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the catcher stands still, the object lands in his hand by the thrower's action alone, so the thrower completed the הנחה and is liable. If the catcher moves toward it, the catcher helped with the landing, so the thrower did not complete the act. The key point is that אחרים count a hand as a valid landing place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name for a תנא (traditionally רבי מאיר)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
Whose opinion is this? It is Acherim.
As it was taught: Acherim say:
If he stood in his place and received it — liable,
if he moved from his place and received it — exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הָא מַנִּי? אֲחֵרִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons the attribution to רבי and offers a new תנא as the source of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution of the משנה to a different תנא

steps.title: Proof that אחרים do not require a four-טפחים area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why אחרים fit the משנה. They make the thrower liable when the object lands in a hand, even though a hand is not four טפחים, so they must not require a מקום ארבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stood in place and caught it, the thrower is liable. But don't we need the object to land on an area of four טפחים, and there isn't one? So learn from this: we do not need an area of four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the inference that makes רבי זירא's suggestion work. אחרים must hold that no four-טפחים area is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually הנחה must happen on a surface at least four by four טפחים. A hand is smaller than that, yet אחרים still make the thrower liable. That shows אחרים do not require a four-טפחים area, which matches our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing down: the end of the act of carrying
An area of four by four handbreadths

phrases.english: He stood in his place and received it — liable,
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the line from the ברייתא in order to analyze it.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בָּעֵינַן הַנָּחָה עַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה
phrases.english: but don't we require placing upon an area of four
and there isn't one!
Rather, learn from this
we do not require an area of four.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ וְקִבֵּל חַיָּיב, הָא בָּעֵינַן הַנָּחָה עַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the first ruling of the ברייתא to draw the inference behind רבי זירא's attribution.
steps.raayaObject: That אחרים do not require a מקום ארבעה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of אחרים that a thrower is liable when the object lands in a stationary hand

steps.title: Maybe only placing doesn't need four handbreadths, not lifting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe אחרים only waive the four-טפחים requirement for הנחה, but still require it for עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is only for placing that we don't need four טפחים, while for lifting we do need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from אחרים. Their ברייתא only shows something about placing, not about lifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the hand is only the landing spot (הנחה). Our משנה also has a case where the object is lifted out of a hand (עקירה). So אחרים do not prove that a hand works for עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting up: the start of the act of carrying

phrases.english: But perhaps it is for placing that we do not require it,
but for lifting we do require it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the inference drawn in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using אחרים to prove a hand is valid for עקירה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא only deals with הנחה, not עקירה.

steps.title: Maybe he caught it in his spread-out garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes further: even for הנחה there may be no proof. Perhaps the catcher spread out the corners of his garment, which made a surface of four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even about placing: perhaps he spread out the corners of his garment and caught it, so there was a real placing on four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא weakens the proof even more. Maybe אחרים do require four טפחים even for הנחה, and the case was a catch in a wide-open garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spread-out garment can easily be four by four טפחים. If the ברייתא describes that kind of catch, it says nothing about a small hand. So אחרים may not support our משנה at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to make אחרים the source of the משנה is rejected on two counts: their ruling may apply only to הנחה, and even that may involve a four-טפחים garment.

phrases.english: And regarding placing as well,
perhaps he spread out the corners of his garment and received it —
so that there is also a proper placing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַנָּחָה נָמֵי, דִּילְמָא דִּפְשֵׁיט כַּנְפֵיהּ וְקַבְּלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rejection from step 6 to cover הנחה as well.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using אחרים to prove a hand is valid even for הנחה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may describe a catch in a spread-out garment that is four טפחים, not in a bare hand.

steps.title: רבי אבא: the object moved from basket to basket
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that the משנה's case involves a basket, which gives a proper four-טפחים surface for both lifting and placing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: Our משנה is talking about a case where he took the object from a basket and placed it on a basket, so there is also a proper placing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives a new answer to the problem of how a hand can count as a proper place for lifting and placing. He says the object was actually in a basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers failed because a hand is not four טפחים by four טפחים. A basket (טרסקל) is big enough, so both the עקירה and the הנחה happen on a proper מקום ארבעה. This means the משנה no longer has to go against the rule that a four-טפחים place is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A basket, big enough to give a surface of four טפחים
Placing or setting down the object, which completes the מלאכה of carrying out

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer lets the משנה keep the normal rule that lifting and placing need a four-טפחים place. It is the basis for the rest of this section.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Our Mishnah is a case where he took [the object] from a basket
phrases.notes: Taking it from the basket is the lifting (עקירה).

phrases.english: and placed it on top of a basket,
so there is also a [proper] placing.
phrases.notes: The placing is on a surface of four טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: מַתְנִיתִין, כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּבֵּל בִּטְרַסְקָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי זירא's answer from אחרים was pushed back, רבי אבא offers a different way to explain the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The object was lifted from and placed into a bare hand, which is smaller than four טפחים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The object was taken from a basket and placed into a basket, which gives a proper four-טפחים surface.

steps.title: But the משנה says his hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's wording mentions a hand, not a basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says "his hand"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא from the wording of the משנה. The משנה says "his hand," not "a basket."
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא's answer depends on there being a basket. The plain words of the משנה describe only a hand, so his explanation seems to go against the text.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it teaches...", a challenge from the exact wording of a source

phrases.english: But it teaches "his hand"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges רבי אבא's answer from the text of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that the case involves a basket
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says "his hand," which does not fit a case about a basket.

steps.title: Reread it as the basket in his hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה should be read as "the basket in his hand."
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: "the basket that is in his hand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבא by rereading the משנה. The person was holding a basket in his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the word "hand" in the משנה, because the basket is in his hand. The object itself still sits in the basket, which gives the needed four-טפחים surface.

keyTerms.meaning: "Teach it as...", an instruction to reread or adjust the wording of a source

phrases.english: Teach: "the basket that is in his hand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the wording challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: "His hand" means a basket held in his hand.

steps.title: A basket in the public domain counts as a private domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a basket held out in רשות הרבים would itself count as a רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for a basket in the private domain. But a basket in the public domain is itself a private domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the basket answer. It works for the homeowner's basket inside the house, but the poor man's basket is out in רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basket held up in רשות הרבים is a raised, enclosed space of four טפחים. That kind of space can count as a רשות היחיד on its own. If so, putting an object into the poor man's basket would not be moving it into רשות הרבים at all.

keyTerms.meaning: "That works fine for...", which sets up a case that does not work

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is the basket being too small. The problem is the opposite: the basket is so complete a space that it becomes its own private domain, even while it sits in public space.

phrases.english: That works for a basket in the private domain,
but a basket that is in the public domain
is a private domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח טְרַסְקָל בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, אֶלָּא טְרַסְקָל שֶׁבִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the basket answer from a different angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basket answer for the case where the object is put into the poor man's hand in רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A basket in רשות הרבים counts as a רשות היחיד. So moving an object from the house into that basket would be private to private, which carries no liability.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the one who treats such a basket as a private domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that the משנה is not like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tentatively proposes (לֵימָא) that the משנה, read with רבי אבא's basket, does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who treats a raised basket as a private domain. The next two steps give the source and the reasoning, and step 15 rejects this proposal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not cancel רבי אבא's basket answer. It suggests that the משנה follows the view that a basket in רשות הרבים is not its own רשות היחיד. The next two steps give the source and the reasoning, and Step 15 then shows that the משנה can fit רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let us say", which introduces a proposed conclusion
A תנא who holds that a raised basket in public space is a private domain

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Let us say it is not like Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This responds to step 11 by saying which opinion the משנה follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a particular opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה works according to every opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (rejected in Step 15).

steps.title: The ברייתא of the basket on a pole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. If someone throws an object onto a basket on top of a pole in רשות הרבים, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, if someone stuck a pole into the ground in the public domain with a basket on top, then threw an object and it landed on it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view. It shows that he treats a raised basket in public space as a רשות היחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thrower is liable only because the object moved from רשות הרבים into a רשות היחיד. That private domain is the basket on top of the pole. So for him, a raised basket in public space becomes its own private domain, even though the pole holding it up is thin.

keyTerms.meaning: "As it was taught", which introduces a ברייתא
Stuck a pole into the ground

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a ברייתא]:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he stuck a pole into the ground in the public domain
with a basket on top of it,
and he threw [an object] and it landed on it, he is liable.
phrases.notes: He is liable for moving it from public to private.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נָעַץ קָנֶה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This brings the source for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view mentioned in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה treats a raised basket in רשות הרבים as a רשות היחיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the basket on top of a pole

steps.title: According to him the homeowner moves private to private
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the משנה cannot follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. For him, the homeowner putting the object into the poor man's basket would be moving it from private to private, so he would not be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it were like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, then when the homeowner stretched his hand outside and put the object into the poor man's hand, why is he liable? He is moving it from a private domain to a private domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning. The משנה makes the homeowner liable, but רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה could not make him liable here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אבא's reading, the poor man is holding a basket out in public. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה treats that basket as a רשות היחיד, so the homeowner moved the object from his private house into another private space. Because the משנה does make him liable, the משנה must not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא explains the משנה as a basket held in the hand, so the four-טפחים rule is kept. The גמרא suggests this means the משנה cannot follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, but the next step answers that it can, because his ruling applies only above ten טפחים.

phrases.english: For if it were like Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
phrases.english: when the homeowner stretched his hand outside
and put [the object] into the hand of the poor man,
why is he liable?

phrases.aramaic: מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד קָא מַפֵּיק!
phrases.english: He is carrying it from a private domain to a private domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This applies the ברייתא from step 13 to the משנה to prove the claim made in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that the homeowner who puts the object into the poor man's hand is liable

steps.title: The basket reading works even for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה after all. His basket was above ten טפחים, while the משנה's basket is below ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: there the basket was above ten handbreadths, and here it is below ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 14. It says the משנה does not have to disagree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה called the basket a רשות היחיד only because it sat high on a pole, above ten טפחים. The poor man's basket in our משנה is below ten, so it is still part of רשות הרבים. That means the homeowner really is carrying from private to public.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (the case can fit even this opinion)
Above ten handbreadths off the ground
Below ten handbreadths off the ground
A handbreadth, a basic unit of measurement

steps.confusionAlert: Ten טפחים is the height at which a raised area can become its own domain. Below ten, the basket is just part of the street.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
there, the basket was above ten handbreadths;
phrases.notes: The pole case quoted in Step 13

phrases.english: here, it is below ten.
phrases.notes: The poor man's basket in our משנה

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim from Step 14 that the משנה must disagree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any basket held in רשות הרבים would be a private domain for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a basket above ten טפחים is a private domain. Below ten it is part of רשות הרבים, so the משנה fits everyone.

steps.title: רבי אבהו objects: the משנה says 'his hand,' not 'basket'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו has a problem with the whole basket reading. The משנה's actual words are 'his hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This was difficult for רבי אבהו: Does the משנה say 'a basket in his hand'? It says 'his hand'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו attacks the answer from Step 10. That answer read a basket into the משנה, but the משנה never mentions one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basket answer only worked by adding a word that is not in the text. רבי אבהו holds that we should not change the משנה's wording when it plainly says 'hand.' So the original problem comes back: how can a small hand count as a proper place?

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach? (a challenge to the proposed wording)
But it does teach (pointing to the actual text)

phrases.english: It was difficult for Rabbi Abbahu:
Does it teach 'a basket in his hand'?
But it teaches 'his hand'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the basket line (Steps 10–15) and returns to the hand problem
steps.kashyaTarget: The basket reading proposed in Step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's text says 'hand,' so adding a basket goes against the wording.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the hand was lowered within three טפחים of the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the poor man lowered his hand to below three טפחים from the ground and caught the object there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבהו said: It is a case where he lowered his hand below three handbreadths and received it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives his own answer for how the hand can count as a valid place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything within three טפחים of the ground is treated as if it is the ground itself. This is the rule of לבוד. So the hand counts as resting on the ground of רשות הרבים, which is a proper place for הנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Below three handbreadths from the ground
The rule that a gap under three טפחים is treated as closed or attached

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abbahu said:
for example, where he lowered his hand
below three handbreadths and received it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected basket reading with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting the case in a specific situation (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hand is too small to count as a place unless it holds a basket.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hand within three טפחים of the ground counts as the ground itself.

steps.title: But the משנה says the poor man is standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה describes the poor man as 'standing,' so how can his hand be that close to the ground?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'standing'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's case by pointing to another word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is standing up normally has his hands far above three טפחים from the ground. So the word 'standing' seems to contradict רבי אבהו's case.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'standing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבהו's case from Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's case of a hand within three טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A standing person's hand is not normally within three טפחים of the ground.

steps.title: Three ways a standing man's hand can be near the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three cases: he is bending over, he is standing in a hole, or he is a very short person.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he is bending. And if you want, say: in a hole. And if you want, say: a dwarf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבהו by offering three different situations where someone 'standing' still has his hand near the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the person is technically standing, yet his hand is within three טפחים of the ground. Bending lowers the hand. A hole lowers the whole person. A very short person's hand is already low.

keyTerms.meaning: A dwarf, a very short person
And if you wish, say (introduces another possible answer)

phrases.english: When he is bending over.
And if you wish, say: in a hole.
And if you wish, say: a dwarf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'standing' challenge from Step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Standing' rules out a hand near the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person can be standing and still have his hand within three טפחים.

steps.title: רבא rejects the forced cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether the תנא would really have gone to such lengths just to teach us these odd situations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Did the תנא go to all this trouble to teach us all these?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רבי אבהו's whole approach, together with its three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bending, a hole, and a dwarf are all unusual cases. It is hard to believe the משנה meant only such strange situations. רבא's complaint is about method: a good explanation should not depend on cases this far-fetched.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Did the tanna go to the trouble of teaching us all these?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the approach in Steps 17–19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אבהו's entire explanation of a hand within three טפחים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It forces the משנה into unlikely, unusual cases.

steps.title: רבא: a person's hand counts as four by four
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a simple rule: a person's hand is treated as if it were a four-by-four טפחים area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: A person's hand is considered for him like four by four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the original problem of how a hand can be a valid place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally עקירה and הנחה must happen on a place that is four by four טפחים. רבא says a person's hand is important enough to count as such a place, even though it is physically smaller. This fits the משנה's plain words with no strange situations.

keyTerms.meaning: Four by four טפחים, the minimum size of a significant place

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the hand is physically four by four. It is treated that way legally for the laws of carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
A person's hand is considered for him
like four by four handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי אבהו's rejected approach with a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hand is too small to be a place for עקירה and הנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person's hand legally counts as a four-by-four place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains every case in the משנה where an object goes from hand to hand. It becomes the basic principle for the rest of the sugya.

steps.title: רבין reports the same rule from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that רבי יוחנן said the very same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, when רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: A person's hand is considered for him like four by four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's rule by showing that רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל taught the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule is not a lone opinion. The same principle was taught by רבי יוחנן, a major אמורא of ארץ ישראל. This makes it the accepted answer to the question of the hand.

keyTerms.meaning: When Ravin came (from ארץ ישראל to Bavel)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: a person's hand counts as a four-by-four place. So handing an object from one domain into another person's hand is a full עקירה or הנחה on שבת.

phrases.english: And so too, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person's hand is considered for him
like four by four handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's rule from Step 21 with an independent tradition
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a hand counts as four by four
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Throwing an object into a friend's hand makes the thrower liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if someone throws an object and it lands in another person's hand, the thrower is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעאי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone threw an object and it landed in his friend's hand, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן. Someone throws an object from one domain to another, and it lands in another person's hand. The thrower is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be חייב for carrying, the object has to come to rest (הנחה) in a proper place. This ruling treats the friend's hand as that proper resting place, so the thrower's act counts as complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, liable to bring a קרבן חטאת)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Elai said
phrases.notes: The ruling is being passed down: רבי אבין heard it from רבי אילעאי, so it comes through two אמוראים.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one threw an object and it landed
in the hand of his friend, he is liable.
phrases.notes: The friend is standing in a different domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'hand is like 4x4' rule from steps 21-22 to a new case: throwing into another person's hand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing an object into another person's hand in a different domain makes the thrower חייב.

steps.title: Why repeat a rule רבי יוחנן already taught?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling as unnecessary. רבי יוחנן already taught that a hand counts as 4x4.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That a person's hand counts as four by four for him? But רבי יוחנן already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the new ruling seems to add nothing. רבי יוחנן already said that a hand counts as a 4x4 place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a great teacher does not repeat himself without a reason. If this ruling is just the old rule applied again, it looks pointless. So the גמרא pushes to find what new idea it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what new idea a ruling adds)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That a person's hand is considered for him
as four by four?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אַמְרַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא?
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan already said it one time!
phrases.notes: Refers to the rule reported by רבין in step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 23 as a repeat of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 23
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the rule that a hand counts as 4x4 was already stated, so the new ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The hand counts even when its owner did not choose to use it
steps.stepSummary: The ruling was needed to show that a hand counts as a resting place even when its owner did not purposely use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that the rule only applies when the person himself made his hand important, by using it on purpose. But when he did not make his hand important, you might say it does not count. So he teaches us that it does count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new ruling teaches something new. The friend's hand counts even though the friend did not choose to make it a resting place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, the person used his own hand on purpose, so you could think the hand counts only because he chose to make it important (אחשביה). Here the object just landed in someone's hand. רבי יוחנן teaches that the hand's status is automatic and does not depend on anyone's intention.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought / I would have said
These words apply (only to this case)
He made it important / treated it as significant
I would say no (it does not apply)

steps.whatToRemember: A person's hand counts as a 4x4 place no matter what. This is true even when its owner did not choose to use it.

phrases.english: You might have said that this applies only
where he himself made his hand important.
phrases.notes: For example, he lifted or received something on purpose.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא אַחְשְׁבַהּ הוּא לִידֵיהּ
phrases.english: But where he did not make his hand important
I would say it does not count.
So he teaches us that it does count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling teaches a new detail (the hand counts even without intent)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hand counts as 4x4 only when its owner purposely made it significant.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hand counts as 4x4 even when the object just landed in it without the owner choosing.

steps.title: The catcher must stay in place for the thrower to be liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the thrower is חייב if the catcher stayed in place. If the catcher moved to catch it, the thrower is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעאי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If he stood in his place and received it, the thrower is liable. If he moved from his place and received it, the thrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a limit to the previous ruling. The thrower is חייב only if the catcher did not move to catch the object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the catcher moves to grab the object, the object did not land on its own from the throw. The catcher's own action finished the job. The thrower did not complete the הנחה himself, so he is פטור.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'liable' and 'exempt' are about the thrower, not the catcher. The catcher's movement decides whether the thrower is חייב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Elai said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he (the catcher) stood in his place and received it, he (the thrower) is liable.
If he moved from his place and received it, he (the thrower) is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to step 23: the catcher must not move.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thrower is חייב only if the catcher stayed in place. If the catcher moved to catch it, the thrower is פטור.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this ruling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting אחרים says the same thing as רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. אחרים say: If he stood in his place and received it, the thrower is liable. If he moved from his place and received it, the thrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן's ruling. A תנאי source, a ברייתא, says exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Showing that a ברייתא already says this gives רבי יוחנן's ruling a firm base in the words of the תנאים. Nothing new is added. The ruling is simply confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)
'Others'; a name for a specific תנא (often identified as רבי מאיר)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a baraita:
Acherim say:
If he stood in his place and received it, the thrower is liable.
If he moved from his place and received it, the thrower is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 26 with a matching ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling about the catcher standing still vs. moving
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of אחרים

steps.title: What if a person throws an object and runs to catch it himself?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks about a person who throws an object, then moves to the other domain and catches it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked: If someone threw an object, then moved from his place, and then caught it himself, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן raises a question (בעיא). The same person who threw the object runs and catches it himself. Is he חייב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one person does both parts: he throws (עקירה) and he catches (הנחה). The question is whether these two moves join together as one complete act of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: He then went back and caught it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked:
If he threw an object and he himself moved from his place
and then caught it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 26: what if the 'catcher' who moves is the thrower himself?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a person חייב if he throws an object and then moves to catch it himself?

steps.title: What exactly is the doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this is a question at all, since one person did the whole act.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן was unsure about. This line sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems obvious that he should be חייב, because one person did both the lifting and the placing. So the גמרא wants to know what the real point of doubt is.

phrases.english: What is his question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's doubt in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the real point of doubt in רבי יוחנן's question?

steps.title: Two forces in one person: one person or two?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains the doubt. The throw and the catch are two separate forces from one person. Do they count as one person (חייב) or as two people (פטור)?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: His question is about 'two forces in one person.' Are two forces in one person like one person, so he is liable? Or are they like two people, so he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה explains what רבי יוחנן was unsure about. The throw and the catch are two separate actions, even though one person did both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two different people do the עקירה and the הנחה, both are פטור, as the משנה teaches; step 26 applies the same idea when the catcher moves. Here the throwing and the catching are two separate efforts that are not one smooth act. So the question is whether we look at the person, which makes it one person and חייב, or at the separate actions, which makes it like two people and פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Two forces (separate actions) in one person
Is considered like / is compared to

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of שני כחות באדם אחד, two separate actions done by one person, is a building block that appears in other areas of הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁנֵי כֹחוֹת בְּאָדָם אֶחָד״ קָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: His question is about 'two forces in one person.'
Are two forces in one person
considered like one person, so he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כִּשְׁנֵי בְנֵי אָדָם דָּמֵי, וּפָטוּר.
phrases.english: or perhaps they are considered like two people, so he is exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 by naming the exact doubt.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubt is whether two separate forces from one person count as one person (חייב) or as two people (פטור).

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle רבי יוחנן's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. It is still unknown whether שני כחות באדם אחד count as one person or as two.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: If a person throws an object and then runs and catches it himself, the law is unresolved (תיקו). This is because we do not know whether 'two forces in one person' count as one person or as two.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in steps 28-30 without a decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of שני כחות באדם אחד stays unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: Catching rainwater in another's courtyard and carrying it out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that one who catches rainwater in his hand inside another's חצר and brings it out is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone put his hand into his friend's courtyard, received rainwater in it, and carried it out, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן about a person who carries rainwater out of another person's חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water fell straight into the person's open hand. The person then moved it to another domain. רבי יוחנן says this counts as a full act of carrying, so he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, liable to bring a קרבן חטאת)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he brought his hand into his friend's courtyard
and received rainwater
phrases.notes: The rain fell into his hand at that moment.

phrases.english: and carried it out, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיקו in step 31, the גמרא opens a new ruling from רבי יוחנן on the same theme of what counts as עקירה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Catching rainwater in another's חצר and carrying it out makes one חייב.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the person did no lifting at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that rain falling into the hand is like a friend placing an object there. In both cases the person did no עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: What difference does it make to me whether his friend loaded him or heaven loaded him? He himself did not do any lifting!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling. He says the person never lifted the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the sugya we learned that if a friend puts an object into your hand, you did not do the עקירה. Rain falling into your hand is the same, since 'heaven' loaded you. Without your own עקירה you should be פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Loaded him (placed the object on/in him)
Heaven (here: the rain coming down by itself)
Lifting the object from its place, the first half of הוצאה

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to it:
What difference is it to me if his friend loaded him,
or if Heaven loaded him?
He himself did not perform a lifting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that he is חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Receiving passively is not עקירה, just as when a friend places an object in your hand.

steps.title: Read 'gathered' instead of 'received'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording. The person actively gathered (קלט) the water, and that counts as עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'he received.' Rather, say 'he gathered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא by changing one word in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קיבל' sounds like he just held his hand still. 'קלט' means he moved his hand and actively grabbed the water from the air. That active grabbing is his own עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say... rather say (a formula that corrects the wording)

phrases.english: Do not say: "He received,"
rather, say: "He gathered."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's קשיא from step 33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He passively received the water, so there was no עקירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He actively gathered the water, which is his own עקירה.

steps.title: Lifting must be from a place of four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that עקירה must be from a place of 4x4 טפחים, and the air is not such a place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need a lifting from on top of a place of four handbreadths, and that is missing here!
steps.whatsHappening: Even with the new word 'קלט,' the גמרא raises a new problem with the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lifting only counts if the object was resting on a real, significant place of four by four טפחים. Rainwater falling through the air is not sitting on any place. So the grabbing should still not count as עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A place of four by four טפחים, the minimum significant surface

phrases.english: But don't we require a lifting
from on top of a place of four handbreadths?
And there is none!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעֵינַן עֲקִירָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that gathering water from the air is a valid עקירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עקירה requires a 4x4 resting place, and falling rain rests on nothing.

steps.title: He gathered the water from the wall
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בריה דרב הונא explains that the water was gathered from the side of a wall, which is a significant place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא, son of רב הונא, said: The case is where he gathered the water from on top of the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the קשיא by placing the case at a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water was not grabbed from the open air. It was running down a wall, and the wall is a real, large place. So the gathering is from a significant place.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; the case is where

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya, son of Rav Huna, said:
It is a case where he gathered it from on top of the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁקָּלַט מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַכּוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 35.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water was grabbed from the open air.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water was grabbed from a wall, which is a significant place.

steps.title: The water never rested on the wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the water only flowed down the wall and never rested there.
steps.simpleTranslation: On top of a wall too, the water did not rest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wall answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עקירה, the object has to be resting on the place. Rain on an upright wall keeps flowing down and never stops. So the wall does not help.

phrases.english: On top of a wall, too,
it surely did not rest!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל גַּבֵּי כּוֹתֶל נָמֵי וְהָא לָא נָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he gathered the water from the wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A place only helps if the object rests on it, and flowing water does not rest on a wall.

steps.title: The wall was sloped
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's idea from another case, the גמרא says the wall was sloped (כותל משופע).
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said that it is a sloped wall, here too it is a sloped wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the wall was slanted, and it borrows this idea from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a slanted wall the water lies on the surface and runs along it, instead of dropping straight down. So the water is considered to be on the wall, and gathering it from there counts as עקירה from a significant place.

keyTerms.meaning: As he said (borrowing an earlier statement)

phrases.english: As Rava said: with a sloped wall,
here too it is with a sloped wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רָבָא בְּכוֹתֶל מְשׁוּפָּע הָכָא נָמֵי בְּכוֹתֶל מְשׁוּפָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further narrowing of the case, based on a parallel ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wall was upright, so the water never rested on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wall was sloped, so the water counts as resting on it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's case is now fully defined. The person actively gathered (קלט) rainwater from a sloped wall in another's חצר and carried it out, so he is חייב.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answers show two separate conditions for עקירה. The person must actively lift the object, and the object must be lifted from a significant resting place.

steps.title: Where did רבא say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבא's sloped-wall statement was originally said, and begins to quote a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רבא's statement said? On what we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote the משנה where רבא first said his sloped-wall idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא used רבא's idea without showing where it comes from. Now it goes back to the original source so we can see the context. The משנה itself appears on the next amud.

phrases.english: And where was Rava's statement said?
On that which we learned in a mishna:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the רבא statement quoted in step 38 by asking for its original source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רבא's statement about a כותל משופע
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was said about a משנה, which the גמרא begins to quote at the end of the amud.
